description.value: The study examined changes in whole-brain functional connectivity following real-time fMRI neurofeedback training of the right inferior frontal cortex in adolescents with ADHD, comparing these changes with training of the left parahippocampal gyrus and relating connectivity changes to clinical symptom changes.

design.value: Randomized controlled trial with 18 adolescents with ADHD receiving right inferior frontal cortex neurofeedback and 13 ADHD adolescents receiving left parahippocampal gyrus neurofeedback as a control. Functional connectivity was compared between the first and last neurofeedback runs.

task_description.value: Each fMRI-Neurofeedback run consisted of seven rest (30s) and six activation (50s) blocks. Rest blocks showed an underwater dolphin image, while activation blocks showed a video-clip of a rocket. Boys were asked to move the rocket towards space by any means they found helpful. They received continuous feedback every repetition time, i.e. 2 s, about their brain activation in their target region of interest via the rocket video-clip.

instructions.value: you can try to concentrate on the rocket or try any other method that works for you

stimuli.value: An underwater dolphin image during rest blocks and a video-clip of a rocket during activation blocks.

task_performance_measures.value: A score (0–10), reflecting the percentage of distance travelled through space during each run

task_description.value: A 5-min fMRI transfer run was conducted after the last fMRI-Neurofeedback run. This was identical to the Neurofeedback training runs, using the same stimuli, but without the feedback, consisting of four rest and three activation blocks.

stimuli.value: The same stimuli as the Neurofeedback training runs, but without feedback.

instrument.value: 3T General Electric MR750 MRI scanner with a 12-channel head coil

description.value: fMRI-Neurofeedback scans were collected using a T2*-weighted gradient echo, echo-planar image sequence. A whole-brain higher resolution gradient echo, echo-planar image scan was also acquired for standard space normalization of individual activation maps.

description.value: A T1-weighted structural scan, used as structural localizer, was collected at the beginning of each scanning session.
fMRI data were first processed to minimise motion related artefacts. After realignment, data were smoothed using a Gaussian filter at 7.8 mm FWHM.

steps.value: A 3D volume consisting of the average intensity at each voxel over the whole experiment was calculated and used as a template.
Each 3D image volume was realigned to this template by rigid body registration.
Data were smoothed using a Gaussian filter at 7.8 mm FWHM.
Correlation data were transformed to standard space using rigid body transformation to a high-resolution echo-planar image and affine transformation onto a Talairach template.

model_settings.value: Average time series were extracted from the seed ROI for each subject and used as a model for a whole-brain correlation analysis producing functional connectivity maps. Group connectivity maps were computed by determining the median correlation coefficient across subjects at each voxel.

estimator.value: non-parametric XBAM analysis with randomization-based voxel- and cluster-wise tests

model_settings.value: Separate repeated-measures ANOVAs tested functional connectivity differences between the last and first fMRI-Neurofeedback run. For group comparisons, run was the within-group repeated measure and group was the between-group measure.

estimator.value: randomization-based tests for voxel- and cluster-wise differences

model_settings.value: Two-tailed Pearson correlation analyses tested correlations between functional connectivity changes and changes in clinical outcome measures.
